In the case filed there for illegal entry, an Indian court acquitted him in 2018, and on 28 February 2023 the appellate court upheld that verdict. He was elected a member of the BNP's national standing committee while he was still abroad.
সুলতানা আহমেদ ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংরক:
Sultana Ahmed is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-17 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the second time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Land.

Sultana Ahmed was born on 26 February 1964. She is the daughter of M. N. Kazi and Nilufa Kazi. She is a businesswoman by profession.

She is active in the leadership of the Jatiyatabadi Mohila Dal and has been a member of parliament before. Her name was on the BNP's announced list of 36 for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament as a former member of parliament. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-17 through the votes of the members of parliament.
সূবর্না সিকদার ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংর:
Subarna Sikder is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-20 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the first time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Religious Affairs.

Subarna Sikder was born on 20 July 1973. She is the daughter of Anil Krishna Sikder and Sova Rani Sikder. She is a former teacher and a leader of the Matua community.

Subarna Sikder is one of the 36 people the BNP nominated for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament, as a representative of the minority communities. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-20 through the votes of the members of parliament.
সেলিমা রহমান ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সংরক্:
Selima Rahman is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-1 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). She is a member of the BNP's national standing committee. In Parliament she chairs the standing committee on the Ministry of Women and Children Affairs.

Selima Rahman was born on 1 September 1941 in Baherchar Khudrakathi village, Babuganj upazila, Barishal district. Her father, Justice Abdul Jabbar Khan, was a former Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan; her mother is Saleha Khatun. Her brothers and sisters include the journalist and columnist Sadeque Khan, the poet Abu Zafar Obaidullah, the journalist and former minister A.Z.M. Enayetullah Khan, and Shahidullah Khan Badal, publisher of the newspaper New Age.

In the BNP she has served as joint secretary general and as vice-chairman. She was a member of parliament from 2001 to 2006, and during that time she served as State Minister for Cultural Affairs.

Selima Rahman is one of the 36 people the BNP nominated for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-1 through the votes of the members of parliament.
সৈয়দ আবদুল্লাহ মোহাম্মদ তাহের ত্রয়োদশ:
Syed Abdullah Mohammed Taher is the member of parliament for Cumilla-11 (Chauddagram upazila) in the 13th Parliament. He has come to Parliament for the second time, from Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, and is Deputy Leader of the Opposition in Parliament. In Parliament he is chair of the standing committee on public accounts. He is also a member of several committees, including the Business Advisory Committee and the standing committee on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. In the party he is a nayeb-e-ameer (deputy ameer), international affairs secretary and a member of the central executive council.

Dr Taher was born into a Syed family in West Dekra village, Alkara union, Chauddagram upazila, Cumilla. His father was an Islamic preacher and scholar; his mother is Aksire Jahan Chowdhurani. As a student Taher won government talent-pool scholarships in class five and class eight, and came third in the SSC examination of the greater Cumilla board. After passing the HSC from Chittagong College in 1975, he obtained an MBBS degree from Dhaka Medical College. As a student he was the elected general secretary of the Dhaka Medical College students' union.

A physician by profession, Taher is associated with various institutions in the healthcare sector. He is the founding chairman of Central Medical College in Cumilla and chairman of Cumilla Tower Hospital and of Al Manar Hospital in Dhaka. He is also the founder of the monthly magazine for children and teenagers Notun Kishorkantha.

He became involved in student politics in his college years. In Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir he served as president of the Dhaka Medical College unit and of the Dhaka city unit, as central general secretary, and as central president for the 1985–86 and 1986–87 sessions. Internationally, from 1988 to 1992 he was Asia director of the International Islamic Federation of Student Organizations (IIFSO), and from 1992 to 1998 its secretary general. During the same period he was director for the Asian region of the World Assembly of Muslim Youth (WAMY). In the 8th parliamentary election in 2001 he was elected a member of parliament for the first time, from what was then the Cumilla-12 seat.

In the 13th parliamentary election held on 12 February 2026, he was elected a member of parliament for the second time, winning 133,308 votes in Cumilla-11 as the Jamaat-e-Islami candidate. His wife, Professor Dr Habiba Akter Chowdhury, is a radiology specialist. The couple have three daughters and a son.
হুমাম কাদের চৌধুরী ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে:
Humam Quader Chowdhury is the member of parliament for Chattogram-7 (Rangunia upazila and the Sreepur-Kharandwip union of Boalkhali) in the 13th Parliament. He has entered Parliament for the first time, for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). In Parliament he is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and of the Library Committee, and chair of Sub-committee No. 1 of the Library Committee.

Humam Quader Chowdhury was born into a political family on 23 June 1983. His father, Salahuddin Quader Chowdhury, was a member of the BNP standing committee and a member of parliament elected from various seats in Chattogram. His mother is Farhat Quader Chowdhury.

Continuing his family's political tradition, he became active in BNP politics and became known through party activities in the Chattogram region. He is a member of the BNP central executive committee.

In the election to the 13th Parliament held on 12 February 2026 he was elected member of parliament for Chattogram-7 as the BNP candidate, winning 101,445 votes with the sheaf of paddy symbol.
হেলেন জেরিন খান ত্রয়োদশ জাতীয় সংসদে সং:
Helen Jerin Khan is the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-9 in the 13th Parliament. She has entered Parliament for the second time on the nomination of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP). She is assistant education affairs secretary of the BNP central committee. In Parliament she is a member of the standing committee on the Ministry of Commerce.

Helen Jerin Khan was born on 17 January 1969, into a politically aware family in Madaripur. She is the daughter of Abdul Latif Khan and Maksuda Khan. In her family, her father and paternal uncles were involved in politics, and her mother was a social worker.

In 1984 she passed the secondary examination from Charmugria Girls' School. In 1993 she obtained a bachelor's (honours) degree in Islamic history and culture from Eden Mohila College. She later obtained a master's degree in political science in 2010 and an LLB in 2012.

Her political journey began in her student days. She was a vice-president of the Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal and was elected vice-president of the Eden Mohila College students' union. In 2005 she became a BNP member of parliament for a reserved women's seat. In the 2008 election she contested Madaripur-2 as the BNP candidate. She is also active in the organisational work of the Jatiyatabadi Mohila Dal. Her name was on the BNP's announced list for the reserved women's seats in the 13th Parliament as a former member of parliament. She became the member of parliament for reserved Women's Seat-9 through the votes of the members of parliament.

She has lived in Madaripur and Dhaka. She is the mother of a daughter and a son.
